messages.author: 96e275f43eafb053
messages.subject: Error in inla.mesh.basis
parts:
Hi All,

I am experiencing the following error from inla.mesh.basis.
basis.T <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="b.spline", n=2, degree=2)
Warning message:
In inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type = "b.spline", n = 2, degree = 2) :
  Old style call for an R2 mesh detected.
  Please supply a 2-element n-vector instead.

 basis.K <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="b.spline", n=2, degree=2)
Warning message:
In inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type = "b.spline", n = 2, degree = 2) :
  Old style call for an R2 mesh detected.
  Please supply a 2-element n-vector instead.

I need help on how to correct it because I have no idea.
I created mesh using the following code

mesh.dummy=inla.mesh.create(loc=borders,extend=list(n=16, offset=0.8),refine=FALSE)
boundary = inla.mesh.boundary(mesh.dummy)
mesh = inla.mesh.create(boundary=boundary,
                        refine=list(max.edge=1.2))

Thanks

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error in inla.mesh.basis
parts:
From
?inla.mesh.basis :

n: For B-splines, the number of basis functions in each
direction (for 1d meshes ‘n’ must be a scalar, and for planar
2d meshes a 2-vector). For spherical harmonics, ‘n’ is the
maximal harmonic order.

so change n=2 to e.g. n=c(2,2) to get a tensor-product b-spline basis.
If that's not what you want, please describe what you do want.

Finn
